witnesses.separates: a three-column L piece: the stored table has no entry for it and the concept is undefined; $DerivedSegments paints a run of the piece's width, three cells; $FixedLengths paints a run of two, as for a two-column L

four L pieces and one bar, so the pipe drops six rows: the stored height keeps 8 rows and leaves the last one blank; $HeightFromPipe makes the frame 7 rows; $WidthFromSteps makes it 9 columns with the source at column 3
five L pieces and one bar: the stored width keeps 7 columns; $WidthFromSteps and $WidthFromInputDiff make the frame 11 columns, the strip's 16 less 5, with the source at column 3
train0's input in a frame 9 columns wide: the stored source column keeps the source at column 3; $SourceCentered puts it at column 4, the center

a strip of three rows holding two three-row bars, with the table holding an entry for a three-row bar: the stored height keeps 8 rows; $HeightFromInput makes the frame 12 rows, four times the strip's; $HeightFromInputDiff makes it 9, the strip's 3 plus 6; $HeightFromPipe makes it 7; $FixedLengths drops two rows per bar
train0's input with a blank column on each side, so 0 outnumbers 2: the stored colors give train0's output; bg=RarestColor takes 2 as the background and fills the frame with 2
train0's input with its pieces in 4: the stored pipe color 2 finds no piece and leaves only the source; pipe_color=DominantColor takes 4, the commonest color, and lays train0's pipe in 4

a piece of two cells that touch at a corner, with the table holding an entry for a one-cell bar: the column-run parse and $Components8 read one glyph the table lacks and are undefined; $ComponentPieces reads two one-cell bars and drops one row for each

a three-row strip whose middle piece has two cells in adjacent columns that do not touch, with the table holding entries for a one-cell bar and a three-row bar: the column-run parse reads one glyph the table lacks and is undefined; $ComponentPieces and $Components8 read a three-row bar and two one-cell bars

a strip whose 2 cells outnumber its 0 cells, with a piece of a one-cell bar that touches an L at a corner, and a table entry for that piece's glyph: the column-run parse and $Components8 read the one glyph and lay its entry; $ComponentPieces reads a one-cell bar and an L; $DerivedSegments reads no bar or L in the glyph and is undefined under $Components8

a three-row strip whose 2 cells outnumber its 0 cells, with a full block, a piece of two cells in adjacent columns that do not touch, and a three-row bar, with table entries for each glyph: the column-run parse reads the two cells as one glyph and drops one row for it; $ComponentPieces and $Components8 read two one-cell bars and drop two rows

the diagonal-contact strip with one cell of 5 in a blank column, so bg=RarestColor takes 5: under $DerivedSegments, $Components8 reads the two cells that touch at a corner as one L and $ComponentPieces reads two one-cell bars, so their pipes differ on a frame of 5
